stem:
Chitra looks at the diagram of a closed shape with three corner points $A$, $B$ and $C$ joined by three straight sides.

Which claim correctly names the shape and its parts?

options.text: The shape is named only by the single corner $A$.
The shape is triangle $ABC$, with sides $AB$, $BC$ and $CA$, and angles at $A$, $B$ and $C$.
The shape is a triangle even if side $BC$ is left open.
The shape is a triangle because the letter $C$ is printed largest on the page.

teacher.key_rationale: A closed three-vertex figure is triangle ABC with three sides and three angles at the vertices. One vertex alone is not the name; an open side fails the closed-shape condition; letter size is not the test.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as labelled triangle ABC with three sides marked.
